approachQuestion.prompt:
Requested Gallery. A non-empty binary tree has unique IDs and an accurate size field on every node: the number of nodes in its subtree, including itself. Given a rank k, return the ID at that position in left-subtree, node, right-subtree order, counting from 1. Numeric IDs are unrelated to rank.

In examples, x(left,right) denotes a node labelled x, and - denotes an absent child. Example 1: Input: 40(70(-,10(-,-)),20(-,-)), k=3. Output: 40; the order is [70,10,40,20]. Example 2: Same tree, k=2. Output: 10. Example 3: Input: 9(-,-), k=1. Output: 9. Size fields, omitted in the notation, are already correct.

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 200000; 1 <= k <= n; IDs are unique signed 32-bit integers. The immutable tree has child pointers and subtree sizes, no cycles or shared nodes. Sizes and child access take constant time. No balance is promised. Only one rank query is requested, and no traversal preprocessing is required.

options.text: At the current node read its left subtree size L, using zero for a missing child. Go left if k<=L, return the current ID if k=L+1, otherwise subtract L+1 from k and go right. Repeat with only a current pointer and rank.
options.feedback: Sizes identify the exact block of ranks occupied by each subtree. One branch retains the requested rank and the discarded block cannot contain it.

options.text: Run a standard explicit-stack left-node-right traversal and stop when the visit counter reaches k.
options.feedback: This returns the correct ID, but enumerates earlier nodes even though supplied sizes let you skip their entire subtrees. Its pending ancestor stack is also avoidable for a single rank descent.

options.text: Compare k numerically with each node ID, going left for smaller k and right for larger k, and return a node whose ID equals k.
options.feedback: IDs are labels, not ranks. Example 1 asks for rank 3 and returns ID 40 even though no ID equals 3.

options.text: Use the left subtree size to choose a child as in rank descent, but keep the original k after moving right.
options.feedback: In Example 1 with k=2, moving right from node 70 must change rank 2 to rank 1. Keeping 2 loses node 10.

feedback.reason: Use supplied subtree sizes to discard whole ranges; the cost of supplied metadata is not new preprocessing.
details: Keep a current node and residual rank. Read L from the existing left-child size, or zero if absent. Return the current ID at rank L+1. Otherwise move left with unchanged rank, or right after subtracting L+1. Repeat until the answer is found. Do not build paths, stacks, or a size table.

The supplied left-subtree size tells how many earlier inorder positions to skip. A right move subtracts those L entries plus the current node; a left move preserves residual rank. Existing size fields are input, not newly allocated workspace.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed iterative rank descent, with existing size fields counted as input. Let h be the tree height in nodes and n its node count. Choose the tight worst-case pair for one query. Count the current pointer, rank and L; exclude the supplied tree and scalar result. The answer can be at depth h-1.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer access, comparisons, arithmetic on the stated integer ranges, and allocation/release of a fixed-size frame take constant time. No hashing is used. Count all live explicit frames; the method does not use language recursion or copy paths/subtrees unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Follow one root-to-answer path using existing subtree sizes and scalar rank.
details: At most one node per depth is inspected, and a target at the end of a chain requires h inspections. Only a constant number of scalar fields is retained.
The left subtree contains ranks 1..L, the node rank L+1, and the right subtree the remaining ranks. Updating the residual rank preserves the unique requested element at every descent.
“O(h) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: At most one node per depth is inspected, and a target at the end of a chain requires h inspections. Only a constant number of scalar fields is retained.
“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: That can describe an explicit-stack enumeration, but this method skips whole subtrees and has no stack.
“O(log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: No balancing promise exists; a valid chain has height n.
“O(h) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: The chosen method is iterative and never needs to return to discarded ancestors, so it stores no ancestor path.
